description:
FILED s417 (Fable), from the Track B1 (#372) probe sweep â the fidelity note
docs/b1-operand-grammar-s416.md Â§2 said to fix in the same commit IF it was one
site.  It is not one site (about ten functions), so it is filed with its
reproducer as the design's other branch says.

PERL'S RULE, probed (perl 5.40.3) â the false value carries information:

    -f "/tmp"          => DEFINED, ""    stat succeeded, /tmp is not a plain file
    -f "/nope-xyz"     => undef          stat FAILED
    -d "/etc/passwd"   => DEFINED, ""
    -z "/etc/passwd"   => DEFINED, ""
    -s "/dev/null"     => DEFINED, 0     <- not "", a real 0
    -x "/etc/passwd"   => DEFINED, ""
    -e "/nope-xyz"     => undef          (-e is 1-or-undef; it never gives "")

PCL answers `nil` (undef) for BOTH cases, because every filetest is written as

    (handler-case (â¦ (if (pred stat) 1 nil)) (error () nil))

which cannot tell a false predicate from a failed stat.

REPRODUCER (diverges for a PLAIN filetest â this is not about stacking):

    my $r = -d "/tmp" && -f _;
    print defined($r) ? "def" : "undef", ":[", ($r // ""), "]\n";
    # perl: def:[]      PCL: undef:[]

    my %h = (k => -f -d "/tmp");
    print defined $h{k} ? "def" : "undef", "\n";   # perl: def   PCL: undef

WHY IT MATTERS: t/op/filetest.t asserts `defined` on exactly these, and any
program that distinguishes "not a plain file" from "no such file" reads the
wrong answer.  It is a SILENT WRONG, not a crash.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the `p--*` family around line 10110 â p--e, p--d,
p--f, p--r, p--w, p--x, p--s, p--z, p--l and the shared %p--stat-test (which
already IS the shared body for the mode-bit tests, so most of the family can
route through one returner).  SHAPE: distinguish the stat call failing from
the predicate being false, and return "" (0 for -s) in the second case.  -e
stays 1-or-undef.  Note -r/-w/-x go through access(2), which conflates the two
differently â check what perl reports for an existing but unreadable file
before writing that arm.

BAR: cl/** change â the full sweep is NOT optional (invisible to corpus-diff),
plus the rows in Pl/t/filetest-stack-01.t whose comment names this task, which
should then be extended to assert definedness.

--- s456ah (Opus agent AH, round 13): THE `-s` MEMBER IS DONE (#740, CLOSED) ---

`-s` is the one member whose answer is a VALUE rather than a flag, so its fix
needed none of the ""-vs-undef machinery this task is about: p--s simply
returned the stat's size unconditionally instead of `(if (> size 0) size nil)`,
and undef now means only "the stat failed".  0 is false to p-true-p, so every
boolean use is unchanged.  Guard: Pl/t/filetest-stack-01.t row 2 (7 lines,
byte-compared against perl 5.40.3, incl. `defined`, `printf "%d"`, the `_`
spelling after an explicit stat, and the `-s -f $E` chain).

THE RESIDUE, RE-MEASURED s456ah on an EMPTY existing file (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL
at 49e55ad + the -s fix) -- these three rows are what is LEFT of this task:

    -z $five_byte_file   perl DEFINED ""    PCL undef
    -x $empty            perl DEFINED ""    PCL undef
    -d $empty            perl DEFINED ""    PCL undef

and matching now, so they are NOT residue: -s $empty (0), -s _ after stat (0),
-s _ after a filetest (0), -s $missing (undef), -s $dir (the dir size),
-e/-f/-z on their true cases, stat()[7].


=== DONE (s473t6b, Opus, 2026-09-17) â commit f70fd153 ===

FIXED, and the task's own "about ten functions, so it is filed" turned out to
be one function after all: the family already had a SHARED BODY
(`%p--stat-test`), so there are FOUR call sites and one returner.

    (defun %p--false ()
      (if *pcl-stat-cache-ok* "" *p-undef*))

`*pcl-stat-cache-ok*` is the flag `%p-stat-buf` and `%p--text-scan` already
maintain -- "did the operation that would fill `_` SUCCEED" -- so no new state
was needed, and `%p-stat-answer` has answered scalar `stat` with perl's `""`
since #1043, twenty lines away.  Call sites: `%p--stat-test` (every mode-bit
test), `%p--access-test` (the stat runs FIRST, so the flag is set before
access(2) is asked), `-T`/`-B`'s scan verdict, and `-t`, which fills no `_`
and answers its two falses from its own errno.  A pred's own 0 (the size `-s`
reports for an empty file, #740) is a VALUE and passes through.

THE SECOND HALF THE TASK DID NOT NAME, and it is the bigger one: CL `NIL` is
not a perl value, so a false filetest left ZERO VALUES in LIST context where
perl leaves ONE.  Measured over all 27 operators -- `() = -d $f` counted 0
here and 1 in perl -- and t/op/filetest_stack_ok.t is 135 rows of exactly
that (`-X returns single value` / `-X *gv returns single value`), 38 of them
blessed failures, the whole file's fail set.

WHAT WAS PROBED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN (perl 5.40.3; probes/p5.pl, p6.pl,
p7.pl in the round's scratch):
  * the task's own note "check what perl reports for an existing but
    unreadable file" -- ANSWERED: chmod 0000, an existing file, perl gives
    DEFINED "" for all six of -r -w -x -R -W -X, and does NOT set $!.  So the
    access arm must ask the flag the STAT set, not access(2)'s own failure.
    (PCL still sets EACCES there -- #1033 made every filetest set $! and
    `-e $f or die "$!"` depends on it.  That is the one residue, below.)
  * `-t` on an OPEN handle that is not a tty is DEFINED "" (ENOTTY); on a
    CLOSED one it is undef (EBADF); both are ONE value.
  * `-M` on a missing file is undef and still one value; `-T` likewise.
  * `-s` on an empty file is a defined 0 (already right, #740).
  * a STACKED run (`-f -d $f`) is DEFINED "" and one value.
  * `-e` is the one member with no middle row -- its test IS the stat -- so it
    stays 1-or-undef and never "".
probes/p5.pl went from 82 differing lines against perl to 3, and those 3 are
the -M/-A/-C ages, which differ run to run.  p6 and p7 are byte-identical.

NO internal CL caller reads these functions (grepped: the only uses are the
`%define-fh-slot-op` definitions), so the #1737 trap -- perl's false is CL's
true -- cannot bite; the `lib/` shims that use `-e`/`-d` are transpiled perl
and see a perl value.

GUARD: Pl/t/filetest-stack-01.t 13 -> 16 rows, a new section 5 (definedness,
list arity, the permission-less file), all three inverse-verified FAILING on a
f26282db extraction.  The file's own "NOT asserted here, and deliberately"
paragraph named this task and now states the opposite (the s416 stale-guard
rule, paid in the same commit).  ir-spec 10c carries the rule as a table plus
the note that a target answering a false filetest with its host's "no value"
is wrong in both readings.

RESIDUE, not this task's: perl does not set `$!` for a false `-r`/`-w`/`-x` on
an existing file (it reads the stat's mode bits and never calls access(2));
PCL sets EACCES.  Left alone deliberately -- #1033 made the family set $! for
`-e $f or die "$!"`, and no measured row asks for the other behaviour.
subject: A filetest's FALSE is undef where perl gives defined-"": the whole p--* family conflates "stat succeeded, predicate false" with "stat failed"
